_doc: Per-person lines read by an outcome's 'people_lines' field (ENCOUNTER_STORIES_DRAFT C18, The Gate, floors 94-98). For each person in the table, the FIRST line whose condition holds is a candidate. A line holds when every key given holds: 'status' (str or list) and 'deserving' (true/false) against deeds['people'][person], and 'when' (a deeds condition, DEEDS 4.3). A person never recorded in deeds['people'] still counts if 'when' holds. Candidates are ordered with the fates first (a line whose status or 'when' names lost, spared or saved), then the most recent first; at most 'max' are told. Never a verdict on the hero; changes nothing mechanical; never touches the floor 99 Judgment. Person ids must match the encounters' 'person.id' and deed ids.

lines.name: Marta Venn
lines.line: Marta Venn walked out on that leg, ratted till she was seventy and never stopped talking about you.

lines.name: Marta Venn
lines.line: Marta Venn's leg held after all, for the most part, though her girl does the climbing now.

lines.name: Marta Venn
lines.line: Marta Venn saw three children on the ward go without while you had her satchel. Then Lena brought home the potions and your apology, and her mother took a week to believe in the apology.

lines.name: Marta Venn
lines.line: Marta Venn got home without her satchel, but three children on the ward never got home. She did not say your name, though Lena did.

lines.name: Ysolde
lines.line: Ysolde and her girl saw Benno's fever break on the eighth night. Ysolde would name nothing after you, but Elara won, and the goat has your name.

lines.name: Ysolde
lines.line: Ysolde and her girl saw Benno's fever break on the eighth night. But Elara told her mother who had the pendant, and so they did not name the goat after you.

lines.name: Ysolde
lines.line: Ysolde and her girl saw Benno's fever break on the eighth night. They named the goat after you, and it is a very nice goat.

lines.name: Dafydd
lines.line: Dafydd and Ilse Marr both got up off that wall, and he went to work in her husband's cheese shop, though the cheese there was terrible.

lines.name: Dafydd
lines.line: Dafydd lived to be sixty, and every winter he told the story of Sergeant Ilse just as it happened.

lines.name: Ilse Marr
lines.line: Ilse Marr went home to her husband and his terrible cheese, and she kept Dafydd's name in her prayers.

lines.name: Father Anselm
lines.line: Father Anselm is back in his parish, and he prays for you on Thursdays, a day of his own choosing.

lines.name: Morrow
lines.line: Morrow made ill use of the freedom you gave him. He will not come through this gate, and he knows why.

lines.name: Konstantin Volkov
lines.line: Konstantin Volkov held the door. He came through here on his feet, and he asked after his farmers first.

lines.name: Jory Pell
lines.line: Jory Pell rose to be a sergeant, and they called him Trembler no longer.

lines.name: Theodoros of Nicaea
lines.line: Theodoros of Nicaea taught six languages free to any who asked, and he would say that a stranger once overpaid for him.

lines.name: Theodoros of Nicaea
lines.line: Theodoros of Nicaea taught six languages free to any who asked, and he would tell of a stranger who broke his chains and wanted no payment for it.

lines.name: Theodoros of Nicaea
lines.line: Theodoros of Nicaea taught six languages free to any who asked. He said a stranger bought him back from a slaver and never asked for the bill of sale.

lines.name: Sariel
lines.line: Sariel asked me to tell you that she hasn't forgotten, for angels never forget.

lines.name: Tansy
lines.line: Tansy walks everywhere now, and hates jars and spoons.

lines.name: Tansy
lines.line: Tansy flies again, hates jars and won't discuss them.

lines.name: Lucan Dray
lines.line: Lucan Dray ran a fifth time and a sixth. When he comes, he and I shall have a very long talk.

lines.name: Lucan Dray
lines.line: Lucan Dray stood his trial and served his years, and afterward he swept the church at Dunmore. Aurel never forgave him, nor was he bound to.

lines.name: Silas Mordaunt
lines.line: Silas Mordaunt added three names before fever took him. The guilt is his, and a little is on the lock.

lines.name: Ostrander
lines.line: Ostrander kept his lamp lit forty years, and people who never knew his name found their way home by it.

lines.name: Ostrander
lines.line: Ostrander went back to his wrecker's trade, and now the sea has him, for it is an unforgiving master.

lines.name: Oswin of Harrow
lines.line: Oswin of Harrow told all of it, Ranulf's part too, and took his sentence without a word. Thale's children lay flowers on his grave, and I call that settled.

lines.name: Oswin of Harrow
lines.line: Oswin of Harrow felled seven hundred and some, by my count, before they stopped him, and he came through still asking to be forgiven.

lines.name: Tobyn
lines.line: Tobyn, knighted at nineteen, carries Brennan's sword and tells his squire far too early that he is ready.

lines.name: Tobyn
lines.line: Tobyn was knighted at nineteen with a borrowed sword, and to his own squire he spoke Brennan's words, every one of them.

lines.name: Celeste Arrowmere
lines.line: Celeste Arrowmere carried Maren home and buried her as was fitting, and every spring she sits with her.

lines.name: Celeste Arrowmere
lines.line: Celeste Arrowmere finished the job, and afterward she went back for Maren.

lines.name: Hal Mercer
lines.line: Hal Mercer and Edwin Corley came through together, and this time it was Hal who went first.

lines.name: Ewan Pryce
lines.line: Ewan Pryce is back in his schoolroom, teaching letters aloud from memory, with his hands in his lap.

lines.name: Ewan Pryce
lines.line: Ewan Pryce went back to his schoolroom and taught the first letters to forty more children, and never once did he speak of the book.

lines.name: Davy Hollins
lines.line: Davy Hollins limped for a year, was made foreman, and first of all pulled out the north props himself.

lines.name: Hans
lines.line: Hans grew up the only child in Hamelin. He became the town clerk, and he read every contract twice.

lines.name: Wat Rowe
lines.line: Wat Rowe lit his six lamps two more winters, and always asked after the stranger who lit the seventh.

lines.name: Ahwere
lines.line: Ahwere asked me to tell you none had ever left the Book before. She said it twice, so I'd get it right.

lines.name: Roland
lines.line: Roland came through still arguing with Oliver, and this once Oliver let him argue.

lines.name: Neferkaptah
lines.line: Neferkaptah waits for his book still, and will go on waiting, as he well knows how.

lines.name: Sir Aldric
lines.line: Sir Aldric went home without the stone and buried Elspeth under the apple tree. He says the truth at her cairn was the first thing that helped.

lines.name: Grumwald
lines.line: Grumwald still minds bridges. His sign says PAY ANYWAY, and under it is written in fresh paint SOMETIMES THEY COME BACK.

lines.name: Ruth Gale
lines.line: Ruth Gale wears her father's amulet and carved his stone herself in the end. She never said whether she forgave you, but I know that she did.

lines.name: Sir Bertilak
lines.line: Sir Bertilak, the Green Knight, hung his girdle on the chapel door. He laughs as he tells all comers that a stranger owned up before he had even lifted the axe, which Gawain never managed.

lines.name: Sir Bertilak
lines.line: Sir Bertilak, the Green Knight, is laughing still about the girdle. He says that you owned up with your own blood running into your collar, and that most people own up no sooner, if they own up at all.

lines.name: Sir Bertilak
lines.line: Sir Bertilak, the Green Knight, says that you called it a fair blow and quits, and that he let you keep his girdle. He asked me to ask you whether it still fits.

lines.name: Sir Bertilak
lines.line: Sir Bertilak, the Green Knight, says that you spoke no word at his chapel and he let you go, and he has yet to decide what your silence meant.

lines.name: Sir Bertilak
lines.line: Sir Bertilak, the Green Knight, says that you drew on him at his own chapel rather than kneel. He has lost his head over less, and he calls it the most honest fight that he has had in a hundred years.

lines.name: Sir Bertilak
lines.line: Sir Bertilak, the Green Knight, waited at his chapel with the axe until the holly had dropped its berries. He says that the girdle went with you, and he hopes that it has kept you warm.
